openings.claim: Material access may cause picking omissions, but the small-batch comparison does not establish this. Evaluate a bounded probe, not a proven intervention for participants and the two assemblers.
openings.delta: Compare shared tagged trays with limited loose materials beside each volunteer while matching patterns, envelope identification and checking.
openings.prediction: With matched patterns and equivalent checks, loose access reduces picking omissions and crossed reaches without increasing total audited assembly time or exceeding table space.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is that pattern mix or omitted checking explains the small-batch advantage: matching these removes the advantage, with omissions persisting during filling despite fewer reaches.
openings.defeat: Equal or more picking omissions under loose access, worse fully audited time, or inability to fit its supplies on the existing table defeats the proposed advantage in this probe; zero errors in both arms is inconclusive.
openings.probe: Use the first twelve production kits as six matched pairs, two pairs per pattern, one kit per layout. Balance layout order and volunteer assignments. Pencil the assigned pattern on every envelope. Tally reaches and compare picked contents before filling with contents after filling against the specified sample; record corrections and all checking, setup and restocking time. Keep every layout within the existing table and count everything inside the same two-volunteer, 90-minute production budget. Use existing envelopes, pencils and materials only.
assumptions: Enough existing material can be staged for the bounded comparison; usable quantities are unverified.
The limited loose layout can fit; measure before starting it.
Inline observation and checking are feasible for the two volunteers without extra assistance.

decision: Run only the bounded comparison that fits the measured table and remaining production budget. Its observations can change which mechanism merits attention; they cannot establish that all 60 correct-pattern kits will be ready within 90 minutes with at most one distribution correction. Current evidence is synthetic stipulation, not tested benefit.

unresolved.issue: Envelope ambiguity may cause exchanges; identification is held constant here, so its effect remains untested.
Full-run restocking, footprint and total checking time remain unproven.
